identificationModule.briefTitle: Effectiveness of Conversion to Sirolimus Versus Calcineurin Inhibitor (CNI) Reduction in Renal Transplant Patients With Prostate Cancer
identificationModule.officialTitle: A Prospective Randomized Pilot Study Examining the Role and Effectiveness of Conversion to Sirolimus Versus CNI Reduction in Renal Transplant Patients With Prostate Cancer

statusModule.whyStopped: Study did not start up as planned.

descriptionModule.briefSummary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the role and effectiveness of conversion to sirolimus versus CNI reduction in renal transplant patients with prostate cancer.
descriptionModule.detailedDescription: This study is designed to support the optimal use of mTOR-inhibitor by providing data for the safe and effectiveness use with sirolimus. This study will take into account effectiveness aspects such as malignancy-free survival cancer by reducing the overall exposure to calcineurin inhibitor.

interventions.name: Sirolimus (Rapamune)
interventions.description: Started at 5 mg (Target levels 6-10mg/mL), Daily, PO, 24 months

interventions.name: Cyclosporin (Neoral) or Tacrolimus (Prograf)
interventions.description:
Cyclosporin: 3-4 mg/kg, BID, PO, 24 months

Tacrolimus: 0-.038-0.045 mg/kg, BID, PO, 24 months

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Renal function as measured by serum creatinine and calculated creatinine clearance (using the formula of Cockcroft-Gault)

locations.facility: McMaster Institute of Urology - St. Joseph's Healthcare Hamilton
